title: Motorcycle traces don't satisfy Lyon stop on first-launched IDs (sequential vs parallel)
description:
PATCH-93 fixed the raycast no-exit-edge precision bug, but uncovered a SECONDARY issue: 75 of 128 motorcycle traces on rocker-arm at alpha=15 now run to MAX_STEPS without satisfying any stop condition. Empirical data: MAX_STEPS aborts dominantly hit LOW motorcycle IDs (0,1,2,4,5,6,7,...). PROPER_STOP IDs are mostly higher (3, 17, 18, 26, ...). Pattern: early-launched motorcycles have no prior traces to crash into; in our sequential launch order they never become a 'crasher' and so cannot satisfy Lyon section 3's both-side alpha-bound stop criterion. PAPER GROUNDING: Lyon section 3 cites EGKT08 (Eppstein-Goodrich-Kim-Tamstorf 2008 'Motorcycle Graphs') for the canonical algorithm. EGKT08 lines 312-323 specify: (a) propagation is parallel/time-stepped ('in a sequence of time steps, move each particle along the edge'), (b) self-stops ARE canonical ('a particle meets a vertex that has previously been traversed by itself or another particle, it stops'), (c) implementation hint uses a hash table H of visited vertices. EGKT08 section 7 line 386 notes: 'the simultaneous movement of the particles is important in making the motorcycle graph CANONICAL but not in generating a CORRECT partition' — so sequential launching can produce a valid partition, but only if traces stop properly via the self-stop / collision rules. Lyon's 'one important difference' (paper section 3 lines 171-175) is the SURVIVAL rule for OTHER-trace crashes; self-stops weren't part of what Lyon modified, so EGKT08's self-stop default still applies under Lyon's framework. FIX: replace our priorId == motorcycleId skip with a proper self-stop. When a motorcycle's ray geometrically intersects its own earlier segment, stop the trace at that intersection (record INTERSECTION node). Skip only the IMMEDIATELY-PRIOR segment in the same face (the one we just came from after a survival crash) — that has t=0 and isn't a real self-crossing.

UPDATE 2026-05-01: self-stop implemented per EGKT08. Result on rocker-arm at alpha=15: 8/75 max-steps motorcycles now terminate via geometric self-crash. The remaining 67 motorcycles do NOT self-cross — they just never satisfy Lyon section 3 both-side alpha-bound stop because they have no priors to crash INTO (they can only ever be victims of later motorcycles, and the victim-perspective alpha is always near pi/2). Self-stop is necessary but not sufficient.

REMAINING ROOT CAUSE: SEQUENTIAL launch order is incompatible with Lyon stop. EGKT08 line 312 specifies parallel/time-stepped propagation. EGKT08 section 7 line 386 notes simultaneous movement is required for canonicalness, not correctness — so non-simultaneous CAN produce a valid partition, but only if every trace stops. With sequential launching, the FIRST motorcycle launched has no priors to crash into; under Lyon-survival rules (without self-stop or boundary), it traces forever.

NEXT FIX OPTIONS:
- Two-pass: Pass 1 trace all motorcycles to natural end (boundary or MAX_STEPS) without applying Lyon stop; Pass 2 retrace each motorcycle using all Pass 1 traces as walls and apply Lyon stop. Lower-effort approximation of parallel.
- True parallel: priority-queue ordered by next-event time (Eppstein canonical). Bigger refactor.

PATCH-94 partial fix: self-stop landed (1 commit). Remaining 67 max-steps cases tracked as PATCH-95 follow-up.
definition-of-done: abort-max-steps drops from 75/128 to under 5/128 on rocker-arm at alpha=15. Motorcycles all terminate via either Lyon both-side alpha-bound stop or EGKT08 self-stop / boundary. tMCG drops from ~14s back toward Lyon paper's 92ms range. Downstream metrics (lost T-junctions, giant DCEL cycle) improve.
testing-plan: 1) Add geometric self-crash detector (raycast against own segments excluding previous step). Count motorcycles that geometrically self-cross. 2) Implement EGKT08 self-stop: when ray hits own segment, terminate trace at that point (record INTERSECTION node). 3) Re-run rocker-arm: confirm abort-max-steps drops. 4) Verify regression suite green. 5) Compare downstream: visible T-junctions, lost T-junctions, giant cycle size, P merged.
